messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — we need a short, customer-facing checklist (one-pager) for onboarding that focuses on caching, batching, and streaming. Goal: reduce early churn by avoiding token surprises and noisy latencies. Can everyone drop a few practical snippets we actually tell customers during kickoffs?

priya: +1. Keep it prescriptive and small. My go-tos: 1) recommend a 30s TTL for edge cache on conversational completions, 2) advise client-side micro-batching for bursty UI actions (batch size 3-8), 3) prefer streaming for perceived latency on chat UIs.

sam: Small additions: include a short "validation harness" customers can run that checks correctness and perf. Example command we give: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"<sanity-test>","max_tokens":64}'` — run 10x and look at median latency + token usage.

jordan: On renewals — capture a simple health signal: 1) % of requests using cached prefixes, 2) median token cost per session, 3) streaming fallback rate (how often streaming falls back to non-stream). If customers see cache hit < 10% after 7 days, flag for follow-up.

priya: For customer-facing wording: "Pro tip: pre-warm frequently used prompts via a daily background job (low-priority) instead of live user requests." Also include an ops-safe script snippet for pre-warm (single curl + small payload).

sam: Suggest we include a tiny code example for client batching (JS):
```
// batcher.js (concept)
let queue = []
function sendBatch() {
  const batch = queue.splice(0, 8)
  fetch('/api/generate', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify(batch)})
}
setInterval(sendBatch, 50) // 50ms flush for low-latency apps
```
Short note: tune interval by p95 latency objective.

alex: Add the streaming safety net: tell customers to set a token budget for fallback path (e.g., if streaming stalls > 300ms, switch to non-stream with limited max_tokens). This prevents endless hanging calls during network flakiness.

jordan: Also include troubleshooting checklist: 1) did you pin model variant? 2) are you using prefix caching correctly (match exact tokenization)? 3) do you observe elevated reroute to fallback region? If yes, check routing policy in console.

priya: For renewal conversations, have CS ask: "Have you seen any unexplained token cost spikes?" If yes, immediately run the validation harness and compare prompt distribution. Provide a pre-canned support path and timeline (24h triage, 72h mitigation plan).

sam: Add a short section on capturing feedback: 1) embed an anonymous 'was this helpful' at end of stream, 2) log first 3 tokens of user prompt and anonymize rest, 3) surface top 5 failing prompts to product weekly.

alex: Perfect. Can one of you assemble into a one-pager (customer language + 3 runnable snippets + a 3-item renewal health dashboard) by EOD? I'll push to the onboarding kit and reference in kickoff templates. :thumbsup:

jordan: I'll draft the dashboard metrics and a sample Grafana query.

priya: I'll write the one-pager copy and the pre-warm curl snippet.

sam: I'll tidy the code snippets and add the validation harness script.

cs-bot: Reminder: create doc in Drive: "CS Onboard — caching/batching/streaming checklist" and set reviewers: priya, sam, jordan, alex.

alex: Thanks team — once live I'll add to the customer kickoff playbook and mark accounts with medium renewal risk as recommended recipients for a proactive health check in week 2. :thumbsup:
